# LLM Arena

> Pit two language models against each other in a structured exchange.
> Pick a fighter, a mask, and a mode; watch them debate, interview, negotiate,
> co-write, or co-author a story; an AI judge calls a winner.

Bring your own OpenRouter key for live bouts. Without one, the arena runs
in Demo mode with a mock script so the UI can be explored without spending.

## The arena

The site is a single page at [/](https://llm-arena.app) with a three-act
flow: loadout → briefing → bout. The loadout uses two pairs of concentric
wheels (inner = model, outer = mask) that the user spins to pick fighters.
The briefing configures rounds, mode, topic, judge model, and judging lens.
The bout streams the two models against each other in real time, then an AI
judge produces a structured verdict (winner, reason, scores per criterion).

## Concepts

- **Model**: an LLM, identified by lab + tier. Tiers map to helmet
  silhouettes (basic / advance / ultra) — pick one of 14 curated models
  across OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta, DeepSeek, and Google.
- **Mask**: a per-side persona that conditions tone (Adversary, Scholar,
  Coach, Skeptic, Storyteller, Strategist, Trickster, or Unmasked). Each
  mask has its own brand color visible across the UI.
- **Mode**: the structural framing of the exchange — debate, interview,
  negotiate, co-write, story. Mode determines turn mechanics (e.g.,
  interview is asymmetric: one always asks, one always answers).
- **Bout**: a complete exchange — N rounds × 2 turns, then a judge model
  scores each side on the user-selected criteria.
- **Verdict**: structured judgment — winner, one-sentence reason, and a
  numeric score per criterion. Persists to bout history (sessionStorage).

## Notes for crawlers

- All bouts run client-side against the user's OpenRouter key.
- Bout transcripts are saved per-session only; nothing is sent to our
  servers. There is no account, no telemetry, no analytics.
- The arena page is heavily interactive (drag wheels, hold buttons,
  keyboard controls) — a static snapshot will not represent the experience.
